_: What each genres & moods label means, for a labeller. The label names are data/genres-moods-vocabulary.json's, the file the classify pass hashes; scripts/genres_moods_enrich.py refuses a vocabulary this file does not define exactly. Subgenres hold the blended subgenres and the themes.

primaryGenres.Action: Spectacle, fights, chases or combat are the dominant mode, including superhero and martial-arts action whose hero fights criminals.
primaryGenres.Adventure: A journey, quest, expedition or treasure hunt drives the story, for a general audience.
primaryGenres.Comedy: Built above all to make the audience laugh. A comedy with horror, crime, action or romance elements is still Comedy.
primaryGenres.Crime: The criminal world is the subject: gangsters, cartels, heists, con artists, or the investigation of a crime by police or detectives.
primaryGenres.Documentary: Non-fiction: documentaries, docuseries, nature and concert films, and unscripted reality, competition, talk or variety programmes.
primaryGenres.Drama: A serious story about characters and relationships where no more specific genre dominates; biopics and historical or war-set dramas are usually Drama.
primaryGenres.Family: Made primarily for children and families: children's and family animation, kids' series, and family films. Choose Family over Adventure, Comedy or Fantasy when the main audience is children and families.
primaryGenres.Fantasy: Magic, mythical creatures or invented magical worlds are central, for an older audience than Family.
primaryGenres.History: The historical event itself is the subject, told as history rather than as one character's drama.
primaryGenres.Horror: Made to frighten: dread, scares, monsters or gore dominate.
primaryGenres.Music: Music is the subject: concert films, music documentaries, and stories about musicians where the music is central. A musical with a story in another genre is not Music.
primaryGenres.Mystery: An unravelling puzzle or whodunit is the core of the story.
primaryGenres.Romance: The love story is the spine of the work.
primaryGenres.Science Fiction: A speculative scientific or technological premise (space, future, aliens, time travel, AI) is central rather than a backdrop.
primaryGenres.Thriller: Relentless suspense and danger dominate and no stronger crime, action or horror identity fits.
primaryGenres.War: The war or combat itself is the subject, told from the battlefield or the war effort.
primaryGenres.Western: Set on the American frontier (or modelled on it): cowboys, outlaws, lawmen, ranchers.

subgenres.Romantic Comedy: A comedy whose plot is a love story.
subgenres.Action Comedy: Action set pieces played for laughs.
subgenres.Dark Comedy: Humour drawn from death, crime, cruelty or taboo subjects.
subgenres.Crime Comedy: Criminals or capers played for laughs.
subgenres.Crime Thriller: The story is a suspense thriller about a crime and its perpetrators or pursuers. Not every film that contains a crime: dramas, comedies and action films with a crime in them are not Crime Thrillers.
subgenres.Action Thriller: A suspense thriller driven by action set pieces. Not action films without sustained suspense, and not thrillers with only a few fights.
subgenres.Psychological Thriller: Suspense from the minds of characters: paranoia, obsession, manipulation, unreliable perception.
subgenres.Legal/Courtroom Drama: Trials, lawyers or courtrooms are central.
subgenres.Medical Drama: Set among doctors, nurses or hospitals, with medicine as the work's subject. Not a single doctor character or an illness in the plot.
subgenres.War Drama: A drama about people living through a war.
subgenres.Historical/Period Drama: A drama set in a clearly past historical period that shapes it.
subgenres.Sci-Fi Horror: Horror arising from a science-fiction premise (aliens, experiments, space).
subgenres.Sci-Fi Action: Action set pieces in a science-fiction setting are the draw. Not a romance or drama that happens to include a robot, AI or future technology.
subgenres.Fantasy Adventure: A quest or journey through a magical or mythical world.
subgenres.Neo-Noir: Modern film-noir: cynical, shadowy crime story with moral ambiguity.
subgenres.Supernatural Horror: Horror from ghosts, demons, curses, possession or the occult.
subgenres.Coming-of-Age: A young person's growth into adulthood is the arc.
subgenres.Police Procedural: Police investigative work, case by case, is the frame.
subgenres.Heist: Planning and executing a robbery is the plot.
subgenres.Serial Killer: A serial killer or the hunt for one is central.
subgenres.Spy/Espionage: Spies, intelligence agencies or espionage missions are central.
subgenres.Assassin/Hitman: A professional killer is a central character.
subgenres.Time Travel: Travel through time drives the plot.
subgenres.Cyberpunk: High-tech, low-life future: hackers, cybernetics, megacorporations.
subgenres.Dystopian/Post-Apocalyptic: An oppressive future society or a world after collapse.
subgenres.Zombie: Zombies or a zombie outbreak are central.
subgenres.Slasher: A killer stalks and murders a group one by one.
subgenres.Werewolf/Monster: Werewolves, giant monsters or creatures are central.
subgenres.Superhero: Superpowered or costumed heroes are central.
subgenres.Mockumentary: Fiction filmed in the style of a documentary.
subgenres.Whodunit/Murder Mystery: Solving who committed a murder drives the story.
subgenres.Biopic: Dramatises the life of a real person.
subgenres.Disaster: A natural or man-made catastrophe and survival of it is central.
subgenres.Sports: A sport, athletes or a competition is central.
subgenres.Prison: Life in or escape from prison is central.
subgenres.Road Movie: A journey by road structures the story.
subgenres.Survival: Staying alive against nature, the elements or a deadly situation IS the plot (castaways, wilderness, disaster, being hunted). Not any story with danger or a fight.
subgenres.Political: Politics, government or political power is central.
subgenres.Musical: Characters sing or dance as part of the storytelling.
subgenres.Narco: Drug cartels or trafficking are central.
subgenres.Hong Kong Action: Hong Kong martial-arts, gun-fu or cop action cinema.
subgenres.Anime: Japanese animation. Only when the work is recognisably Japanese animation.
subgenres.Gangster/Mob: Organised crime families or gangs are central.
subgenres.Cult: Widely known as a cult classic. Only if the work is recognisably one, never from plot alone.
subgenres.Christmas/Holiday: Christmas (or another holiday) is the work's occasion and theme, as in a Christmas film. Not a story that merely passes through a holiday.
subgenres.Faith & Spirituality: Religious faith or spirituality is central, often made for a faith audience.
subgenres.LGBTQ+: LGBTQ+ characters, relationships or identity are central.
subgenres.Art House: Known as an art-house or festival film. Only if the work is recognisably one.
subgenres.Epic: Recognised as an epic: vast scale, long span, grand sweep. Only if the work is recognisably one.
subgenres.Body Horror: Horror from the grotesque transformation or violation of the body.
subgenres.Found Footage: Presented as recovered recordings made by characters.
subgenres.Folk Horror: Horror from rural isolation, pagan rituals or folklore.

moods.Slow-burn: Tension or story builds deliberately over time toward a payoff; patient pacing.
moods.Feel-good: Leaves the audience uplifted and happy; a warm, positive resolution.
moods.Mind-bending: Plays with reality, time, memory or perception; puzzling concepts.
moods.Cozy: Gentle, warm and low-stakes: small communities, familiar routines, light mysteries.
moods.Dark & Gritty: Bleak, violent or morally grim throughout, in a harsh realistic register. Not every story with a death or a crime.
moods.Wholesome: Gentle and good-hearted throughout, with no cynicism, cruelty or menace worth warning a parent about: made for all ages. Not every film with a happy ending.
moods.Tearjerker: Built to make the audience cry: loss, sacrifice, grief.
moods.Tense/Edge-of-seat: Suspense and danger are sustained through most of the work and are its main experience. Not a story with a few tense scenes.
moods.Quirky/Offbeat: Eccentric characters or unusual humour and style.
moods.Visually-stunning: Striking visuals are a central draw: spectacle, cinematography, animation or effects.
moods.Twist-ending: A major late reveal recontextualises the story.
moods.Bingeable: A serialised TV series whose cliffhangers and ongoing mysteries are its main pull. Never a film; not episodic, procedural or anthology series; not every popular show.
moods.Comfort-watch: A light, familiar, low-stakes favourite people rewatch to relax: sitcoms, cosy procedurals, family classics. Not anything with sustained tension, darkness or grief.
moods.Thought-provoking: Built around ideas: it deliberately poses moral, social or philosophical questions the audience is meant to keep thinking about. Not every serious drama.
moods.Steamy/Sensual: Sexual tension or erotic content is central.
